result: Shamsi rejected all four. Every build used the design system's parts correctly, but none worked out the hierarchy the pages need: all four organised the sample data (tables on the two doorway pages, alerts and status lines above the content) instead of deciding what is primary. Two design-system problems showed up: a table's scroll wrapper let hidden header text widen the page on a phone (fixed: .ds-table-scroll is now positioned), and the card grid ran past a 360px screen (fixed 2026-10-07). All four used the light header that the docs pages themselves use.

A.notes: No page CSS. The report's parts and views are a sidebar of accordions, which is not what the sidebar is for. Two landmarks share a name on the sections page.

B.notes: Seven rules on tokens: the views as a row of links with the current one marked, and the period line. Report parts in .ds-subnav.

C.notes: No page CSS. Parts and views in a sidebar of accordions; the secondary navigation changes from page to page. Two landmarks share a name on the sections page.

D.notes: Eight rules on tokens: .ds-subnav reused for the views inside the page, a status row, IDs in mono.

patterns: All four used .ds-internal, the light header, .ds-card--stat for totals, tables for the two doorway pages, an alert for groups that need attention, and chart placeholders as asked.
No build used .ds-tabs. Two put parts and views in sidebar accordions; two used .ds-subnav for the parts and a row of links or a second .ds-subnav for the views.
All four put status lines, refresh and alerts above the main content.
Design-system bugs: .ds-table-scroll was not positioned, so is-sr-only text in sortable headers widened the page (fixed); .ds-card-grid's 20rem minimum (fixed 2026-10-07).
Predictions: 1 right (all .ds-internal). 2 right (all four used .ds-card--stat). 3 partly: they split, but between sidebar accordions and secondary navigation, not tabs.
findings: The builds organised the data instead of the page: there is no guidance on telling a doorway page (choose where to go) from a working page, or on keeping secondary content from pushing the main content down.
There is no pattern for navigation with two levels (a report's parts, then its views), so each build invented one.
All four copied the light header from the docs pages, which use it for their own navigation.
next: Write guidance for page hierarchy and doorway pages, settle two-level navigation, then build again with the data replaced by placeholders.
